label: Avaśya Rakṣibe Kṛṣṇa Song Four
title: choḍato puruṣa-abhimān
metaDescription: Avaśya Rakṣibe Kṛṣṇa Song Four: (choḍato puruṣa-abhimān) of Śaraṇāgati (‘Surrender’) written by Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura in 1893. This songbook contains 50 songs detailing the six symptoms of surrender unto the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

verses.translation: I give up the vanity of the error that I am a male. Today I have become Your faithful maidservant, O Kāna!
In the groves of Vraja I will render personal service as a follower of one of the confidential sakhīs, O Lord of Rādhā!
I will string together a garland of forest flowers, in which tulasī buds shall be the jewelled pendants.
With utmost care I will place the garland in the hands of my superior sakhī, and she will take it out of my hands with loving regard.
Then she will place the garland around both of Your necks, while from afar I watch in wonder.
The confidante will then say to me, “Listen, O beautiful one, you shall remain in this grove as my attendant.
“Daily you will string together beautiful flower garlands that will enchant Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.
“The responsibility for your maintenance is mine. My cottage in this grove is yours.
“When the time comes for me to go and serve Rādhā and Mādhava, you will stay close to me while remaining hidden.
“After dressing packets of betel nuts and fetching the camphor, you will hand them to me, knowing me to be your very own.”
Bhaktivinoda, having heard all these instructions, bows down at the lotus feet of that confidential sakhī.
